title: Match mixed newline conventions deliberately
goal: Apply regex anchors and dot to CRLF, CR, LF and Unicode line separators with an explicit newline policy.

selectionNotes: Add AnyNewLine explicitly; Multiline controls anchors and Singleline still lets dot consume separators. Normalized input has different source offsets.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: This edition uses .NET 11 library APIs; the .NET 10 code is a comparison, not a catalogue route.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Build the declared net11.0 sample with the .NET 11 SDK.

language.name: C#
language.reason: The canonical net11.0 project selects the .NET 11 default C# 15 language mode.

prerequisites: Use a net11.0 console project with LangVersion=15.0. Include the imports stated in the recipe.
constraints: AnyNewLine changes authored regex newline handling; generator/code-fixer improvements are not extra APIs or automatic fixes to existing patterns. Multiline controls anchors and Singleline controls dot: Singleline still allows dot to consume line separators. The test checks this interaction and seven mixed-ending records. Preserve timeout/security policy for untrusted complex expressions; this small fixed pattern is not a general log parser. Normalization and direct matching can produce equal line values while retaining different source offsets. Do not promise the older normalized offsets equal the original positions.
stabilityLimitations: RC2 verification; GA reconciliation remains pending.

evidence.scope: Actual UnicodeText compilation and focused execution on Windows. No mocks, cross-compilation, native deployment or GA proof.
